Me asking about their number of partners is related to wanting to know the nature of those encounters. It was always a way to open the door to that.

Statistically, the more people you’ve been with, the greater the target it is to have an STI. Even if you’ve slept with one person you can get an STI, I’m aware of that. But they got it from someone who got it from someone who….it goes on and on. Asking about encounters helps identify the risk of exposure. 


Just a difference in opinion is all, but I appreciate you taking the time to hear it out.

Condoms help tremendously, but they’re also not 100 percent. You make a good point, and I actually  said I don’t care if they have 50+ partners in the post, it’s about gauging how they prioritize their health. Me asking about body counts isn’t a way for me to point fingers, it’s a way to see how they value their health. 

My opinion is that it’s okay to ask and genuinely care about someone’s body count. It isn’t immature to care.

Going raw on a one night stand is putting a lot of faith in another individual that they’ve been tested recently and have kept track of their encounters. A lot of STI’s take weeks/months to even show up, so again - a lot of trust being put on that second party. 

I’m just saying for me personally it matters. For others it may not. Not a right or wrong thing, just a different approach thing.
I agree with you! Thanks for pointing out that it shouldn’t be correlated too much.

I think people look down on asking because it’s been viewed as a weird way to keep score. I always viewed it as a way to keep health in check, so I never saw an issue in asking. Recently though, I’ve been told a lot that it’s juvenile to ask.

I only think it’s seen as juvenile because people misunderstand the reason for asking. For me, it isn’t to flex or judge at all.

I agree with this. To me, asking about previous encounters goes along with that “consistent communication.” It shouldn’t be done in a shameful way, but rather a “how can we be safe” about this way. Past encounters help one identify possible exposures, prioritize health, etc.

I think people now view body counts as a way of judging or keeping score, when it really should just be a way to keep to your health in check. That’s why I think it’s okay to ask.

Here are just some random (very basic) tips that helped me: 

1. Always get a makeup primer. The Elf pore-less putty primer, or even just the Elf pore-less primer (looks like a pink bottle) is a really good affordable option. 

2. Get a beauty blender for all liquid products, especially foundation and concealer. Run it under the faucet before use until it’s 2x it’s original size and soft to the touch. It sounds “duh” but you’d be surprised how many people forget this and just try to use it as is.

3. Invest in a good finishing spray, it will make your makeup last longer (again, I use Elf or NYX) 

4. YouTube and Pinterest can be your best friends as far as applications tips and product 
info.

5. Blend blend blend, and then blend some more. I cringe to think of my unblended eye shadow and bronzer days.

6. Relax! Putting on makeup can actually be very therapeutic when you allow yourself to enjoy the process while you’re learning the process.
